title: Iran's Hormuz blacklist reshapes flows, but exports hold
section_path: Iran's Hormuz blacklist reshapes flows, but exports hold
section_path_text: Iran's Hormuz blacklist reshapes flows, but exports hold
summary:
Main
Despite Iran blacklisting more than half the Gulf shuttle fleet, oil flows continue to grow as tankers adapt through additional STS transfers. By Claire Jungman
Iran has designated more than half the tankers involved in Gulf shuttle operations, but so far the restrictions have not reduced the volume of oil moving through the shuttle relay. Instead, Vortexa data indicates that operators are adapting how cargoes move, with some designated vessels relying on an additional ship-to-ship (STS) transfer to get oil to its final destination.

children.title: Iran's designations now cover the majority of shuttle activity
section_path: Iran's designations now cover the majority of shuttle activity
children.section_path_text: Iran's designations now cover the majority of shuttle activity
children.summary: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) expanded its Non-Compliance List on 2 November, adding 114 vessels and bringing the published total to 240. Of the 231 tankers Vortexa has identified as participating in Gulf shuttle operations since March, 130 were included in that version of the list, representing 56% of the fleet.

children.title: Iran has targeted the busiest ships, not one exporter
section_path: Iran has targeted the busiest ships, not one exporter
children.section_path_text: Iran has targeted the busiest ships, not one exporter
children.summary: What sets the designated tankers apart is how active they have been in the relay, not where they load. Only 26% of tankers that made a single shuttle run since March are on the list, against 86% of those with four to six runs and 89% of those with seven or more.

children.title: Additional STS transfers are emerging in cargo movements
section_path: Additional STS transfers are emerging in cargo movements
children.section_path_text: Additional STS transfers are emerging in cargo movements
children.summary: One of the more notable developments is the increasing use of additional STS transfers involving designated vessels. For shuttle tankers designated by 14 September, Vortexa estimates that the share of relayed barrels involving a second STS transfer increased from 17% in June-July to 21% between 15 September and 25 October.

children.title: What does this mean for Gulf oil exports?
section_path: What does this mean for Gulf oil exports?
children.section_path_text: What does this mean for Gulf oil exports?
children.summary: The data so far suggests that Iran's restrictions are having a greater impact on how oil moves than on how much oil moves . Designated tankers continue to load Gulf crude, and overall shuttle volumes have increased even as the number of vessels on the PGSA list has expanded.
